bundestag.summary:
SUMMARY:
This document is the stenographic report of the 78th session of the 21st legislative period of the German Bundestag, held on Friday, May 8, 2026. The session covered a variety of agenda topics. A significant portion of the discussion revolved around **Agenda Item 22**, which involved the second and third readings of a government bill to introduce electronic monitoring of residence and perpetrator work within the Domestic Violence Protection Act. This was discussed in conjunction with **Supplementary Agenda Item 12**, a resolution proposal from Die Linke advocating for a comprehensive strategy against domestic and gender-based violence instead of isolated measures. Debates on this topic featured contributions from Carmen Wegge (SPD), Rainer Galla (AfD), Dr. Günter Krings (CDU/CSU), Dr. Lena Gumnior (BÜNDNIS 90/DIE GRÜNEN), Aaron Valent (Die Linke), Tobias Matthias Peterka (AfD), Stephan Brandner (AfD), Susanne Hierl (CDU/CSU), Marcel Emmerich (BÜNDNIS 90/DIE GRÜNEN), Ulle Schauws (BÜNDNIS 90/DIE GRÜNEN), Kathrin Gebel (Die Linke), Carsten Müller (Braunschweig) (CDU/CSU), Lisa Paus (BÜNDNIS 90/DIE GRÜNEN), Helge Limburg (BÜNDNIS 90/DIE GRÜNEN), Knuth Meyer-Soltau (AfD), Josephine Ortleb (SPD), Tijen Ataoğlu (CDU/CSU), and Axel Müller (CDU/CSU). Minister of Justice Dr. Stefanie Hubig (BMJV) also spoke on this matter.

Another major topic was **Agenda Item 23**, which began with the first reading of an AfD bill to abolish the Wind Energy Area Requirements Act (WindBAG). This was followed by an AfD motion for a nationwide moratorium on the expansion of wind energy. Speakers on these items included Christian Reck (AfD), Dr. Maria-Lena Weiss (CDU/CSU), Katrin Uhlig (BÜNDNIS 90/DIE GRÜNEN), Dr. Paul Schmidt (AfD), Dunja Kreiser (SPD), Lorenz Gösta Beutin (Die Linke), Michael Kießling (CDU/CSU), Leif-Erik Holm (AfD), Helmut Kleebank (SPD), Dr. Alaa Alhamwi (BÜNDNIS 90/DIE GRÜNEN), Dr. Ingo Hahn (AfD), Jörg Cezanne (Die Linke), Lars Rohwer (CDU/CSU), Carolin Bachmann (AfD), Dr. Paula Piechotta (BÜNDNIS 90/DIE GRÜNEN), Angelika Glöckner (SPD), Elisabeth Winkelmeier-Becker (CDU/CSU), and Karsten Hilse (AfD).

**Agenda Item 24** concerned a motion by the CDU/CSU and SPD factions to designate 2026 as the "Day of Urban Development Promotion" to foster strong cities and municipalities. Finally, **Agenda Item 25** encompassed five motions from Die Linke aimed at strengthening works council co-determination rights, improving their working conditions, promoting works council formations, protecting them from anti-co-determination employers, and enhancing co-determination at a multinational level through reforms of European Works Councils. Contributions on these latter items came from Cem Ince (Die Linke), Peter Aumer (CDU/CSU), Pascal Meiser (Die Linke), Hans-Jürgen Goßner (AfD), Angelika Glöckner (SPD), Ruppert Stüwe (SPD), Volker Scheurell (AfD), Dr. Katja Strauss-Köster (CDU/CSU), Sylvia Rietenberg (BÜNDNIS 90/DIE GRÜNEN), Katalin Gennburg (Die Linke), Hendrik Bollmann (SPD), and Bastian Treuheit (AfD).

UKRAINIAN MEN:
No discussion about Ukrainian men found in this session.

facts.fact: During the height of the Roman Empire, purple dye was incredibly expensive and difficult to produce, requiring thousands of sea snails for just a small amount of dye.  This rarity led to purple becoming a symbol of royalty and power, so much so that only emperors and high-ranking officials were permitted to wear it.

The tradition of the 'kissing the ring' gesture in Catholicism, often seen with bishops and the Pope, originates from ancient Roman customs where subjects would kiss the rings of powerful officials to show deference and loyalty. This practice was adopted by the early Church as a way to signify submission and respect for ecclesiastical authority.
